rss.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement. In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use: We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it. Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks. OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News: In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select. Here are the pelicans for the different reasoning levels. rss.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
rss.summary: How Greptile uses GPT-6 Astra to test user workflows, Daybreak to strengthen security, and Codex to reduce rework.
rss.text_excerpt:
Greptile ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds AI agents that review and test code changes with full context of the codebase. “We are in the business of reducing bugs and making the world’s software more reliable,” says Co-founder and CEO Daksh Gupta. For Daksh, that mission requires testing an application’s behavior as well as reading its code, and GPT‑6 Astra’s computer use gives Greptile a way to automate testing at scale. Validating a pull request involves checking whether the code is logically correct, does what the developer intended, is secure, and avoids breaking existing functionality. For some of that testing, you need to actually run the application because reading the code alone might not reveal the problem. Daksh gives the example of a button that disappears when a website is viewed on an iPhone. With GPT‑6 Astra, Greptile can start a development server for a pull request, resize the browser to an iPhone-sized viewport, and simulate a user moving through the application. The model’s visual understanding lets it inspect the screen and spot the hidden button. “A QA firm testing all of your changes is just impractically slow considering how fast we’re able to ship code with these models,” he says. With GPT‑6 Astra, Greptile can automate this kind of application testing at scale. Daksh says more powerful models also make it easier for attackers to exploit applications, putting companies at risk, even those that previously would not have been typical targets. “We want to make it very easy for even a startup to secure their systems,” says Daksh. “With Daybreak, we’re able to do this in a way that is very safe, and we can ensure that our customers have more sophisticated defense mechanisms than the adversaries have offense mechanisms.” Greptile’s Knowledge Base indexes a company’s codebase and documents how it works in a form people and agents can read. The company makes that documentation available to Codex through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. This allows Codex to write code that follows the customer’s existing patterns, and thousands of customers have connected Codex to Greptile’s knowledge base, according to Daksh. To measure the impact, the team tracks how often AI-generated code is reverted. “When we provide agents with context, fewer reverts happen and customers save time and save inference,” Daksh says. rss.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
rss.summary: OpenAI shares model results on the Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics—and how researchers can verify and build on them.
rss.text_excerpt:
We are announcing three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics about harmonic analysis, complexity theory, and quantum field theory. Our release process continues to evolve in response to feedback from the associated academic communities. In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data. To convert this raw research data into scientific understanding, in this release we are experimenting with a new approach. We reached out to external experts and asked them to act as shepherds, organizing groups to understand the new results. They advised three different release strategies: For the math result, release the AI output, leaving researchers free to organize their own efforts to explain the result. For the computer science result, form an external group of collaborators to explain the result, while making the AI output publicly available for anyone to examine and build on. For the physics result, form an external group of collaborators and defer to them on the release of materials. We do not yet know which of these three approaches will be most useful, and we welcome feedback on what works and what we can improve. The external collaborations will follow four principles: Transparency. We are transparent about the existence of our collaborations. Participants will not be asked to sign nondisclosure agreements and will be free to discuss the work, share intermediate products, and publish their conclusions. No Academic Credit. We do not seek academic credit for the discoveries produced by our internal models. Inviting a researcher to help steward a collaboration also does not imply that they or their working group made the original discovery. Recognition. This group should receive recognition for the understanding they develop, the writeups they author, and the other materials they create. The group will also help ensure that the work appropriately credits researchers, techniques, and ideas that it draws on. Independence. Participation is voluntary and unpaid. Working-group members participate independently, and their conclusions are their own. They do not speak on behalf of OpenAI, and OpenAI does not speak on their behalf. rss.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
rss.summary: CodeRabbit uses GPT-6.1 Sol to investigate security risks across complex codebases. Its security agent helps developers review findings and proposed fixes.
rss.text_excerpt: As AI accelerates software development, engineering and application-security teams need ways to investigate code changes and address vulnerabilities while keeping people in control. CodeRabbit is using GPT‑6.1 Sol as the primary model in its security agent to extend review beyond individual changes and help developers understand risks across complex codebases. A pull request can affect shared libraries, dependencies and safeguards elsewhere in an application. GPT‑6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit connect behavior across files and components to surface potential security issues. CodeRabbit’s review is independent of the agent that wrote the code and complements established scanners. Its system also uses other frontier models and security tooling. During pull-request review, Sol helps analyze changes as developers work. In Deep Scan, it supports broader investigation across repositories, including dependencies and how components interact. CodeRabbit Secure extends that investigation to linked repositories, such as a shared authentication library, to help teams understand how a weakness could affect the wider system. CodeRabbit reports using GPT‑6.1 Sol to flag security-related issues across thousands of repositories and organizations. These findings feed into the pull-request workflows developers already use to review and improve their code. CodeRabbit Secure connects investigation to remediation. For user-selected findings, it can attempt exploit verification in an isolated sandbox without testing production systems. For supported issues, it can draft a pull request with a proposed fix for a person to review and approve. This work shows how frontier reasoning can support software security: understanding risks beyond an individual change, helping validate findings and turning them into proposed fixes. Human reviewers remain responsible for deciding which changes to ship. Learn more about GPT‑6.1 Sol here . Learn more about CodeRabbit Secure here ⁠ (opens in a new window) .

rss.summary: Explore OpenAI Signals data on 165 work activities across nearly 100 countries, revealing how people use ChatGPT for work and how usage changes over time.
rss.text_excerpt:
Today, we are releasing OpenAI Signals data that explores 165 work activities across nearly 100 countries, revealing how consumers use ChatGPT for work. This data gives researchers a new way to study AI’s role in the economy, with new information on the work activities people bring to ChatGPT—from preparing instructional materials and developing marketing content to programming and analyzing business data. Researchers can use this data to explore how ChatGPT use for work differs across countries, track changes over time, and match this data to other economic indicators. The release connects ChatGPT usage to 165 work activity categories called Intermediate Work Activities (IWAs). IWAs are commonly-used categories of tasks for the kinds of work people do across occupations. The data is represented quarterly, spanning a period from the first quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of 2026. Our new data draws on O*NET, a standardized framework that groups occupation-specific tasks into broader categories of work activities shared across occupations. Using a common framework helps researchers compare ChatGPT use with other types of occupational and employment data. The interactive chart below can be used to explore these work activities within a specific country over time, moving from broad activity groups to more specific activities. The data shows wide variation across countries in how people use ChatGPT for work. Connecting this data to IWAs revealed that work-related use became less concentrated in the most common activities. That means that countries tended to specialize in their work over time, and different countries specialized in different types of work. These differences might reflect variation in the kind of work done across countries or varying access to AI tools. Exploring these questions is one example of many that researchers can pursue with this new data. rss.title: How Fanatics and OpenAI streamline the fan experience
rss.summary: Fanatics uses OpenAI to help fans complete their game-day outfits with Shop the Look. Testing across roughly 30,000 MLB products showed 10% higher engagement.
rss.text_excerpt: Fanatics and OpenAI are collaborating to improve the fan experience. As part of that work, Fanatics is launching an OpenAI-powered version of Shop the Look, which uses AI models to recommend coordinated merchandise to help fans complete their game-day outfits. Fanatics, a global digital sports platform, uses ChatGPT Work and Codex across Fanatics Corporate, Commerce, Collectibles, and Betting and Gaming. Shop the Look is now live across many sites across the Fanatics network—including Fanatics.com and the official NFL, NBA, MLB and NHL online stores. With it, fans can more easily find recommended merchandise to match with items they’re looking to wear. When fans browse for their favorite team’s jersey, Shop the Look suggests coordinated outfits on the product page, using in-stock items that match their team and intended style. OpenAI models draw on enriched product data, team and inventory information to assemble the recommendations. Fanatics’ merchandising rules keep the selections compatible and relevant, and looks are refreshed daily as catalogs change. Using Codex, OpenAI and the Fanatics engineering team quickly developed custom recommendation tools to enrich product and catalog data, find compatible merchandise, evaluate recommendations, and generate looks for each product. Testing the new approach on 50 products took less than a day to complete. Fanatics reviewed the looks and gave feedback directly to the builders. After a couple days of iteration, the company approved the minimum viable product that same week. OpenAI helped design the solution which enabled Fanatics to implement the new Shop the Look experience in their production environment and scale the approach across thousands of products. After testing the recommendations across roughly 30,000 MLB products, the OpenAI-powered Shop the Look experience achieved 10% higher engagement than the previous experience. We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra continues to advance the cost-intelligence frontier across our model families, providing a new balance of speed, capability, and cost. Its standard API prices are 50% lower than those of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, making it practical for developers to automate high-volume work, like reading incoming invoices and entering their details into accounting software. In ChatGPT Work and Codex, your plan goes further with GPT-6.1 Terra—the same usage allowance covers more tasks than with GPT‑5.6 Terra and substantially more than with GPT‑6.1 Sol or GPT‑6 Astra. From visual understanding to action We measured GPT-6.1 Terra’s computer-use capabilities on Agents’ Last Exam, a benchmark of professional tasks that includes turning architectural drawings into a 3D model and reviewing an animated film shot by shot to create a time-coded log for a restoration team. On MMMU-Pro , a benchmark of visual reasoning, GPT-6.1 Terra outperforms GPT-5.6 Terra at every reasoning setting. 为人与 Agent 协作而生的一站式科研工作台

保留人类舒适的 PDF 阅读习惯，为模型提供纯净的结构化上下文；文献、笔记与交互记录统一沉淀于本地。

中文 | English

如果本项目对你有帮助，请在右上角**给个 star** 吧！

--- ## 背景与设计初衷 Zotero 是学术管理领域非常优秀的软件。它功能成熟、生态稳定，帮助许多科研人员建立了最初的文献归档体系。 但在当下日常科研与深度使用各类 Agent 时，传统的文献工具链暴露出一些断点： * **上下文严重分散**：论文存储在 Zotero，笔记记在 Obsidian，与模型的推导和分析留在各个网页对话框中。三者数据彼此隔离，当需要 Agent 结合某篇具体论文与历史笔记进行深入推导时，用户必须反复手动复制粘贴。 * **文献格式对模型不友好**：人类习惯阅读排版良好的 PDF 文件；但对于模型而言，直接解析双栏排版、跨页表格、复杂数学公式和交叉引用的成本极高，极易产生识别错误与幻觉。结构化 Markdown 与 LaTeX 才是模型容易准确理解的格式。 * **维护成本较高**：AI 伴读、全文翻译、笔记同步等高频需求，往往需要安装和调试多个社区插件，配置门槛高且在版本升级时容易出现兼容性问题。 * **批量自动化能力有限**：通过 Deep Research 或自动化检索工具发现的大量文献，目前仍需人工在浏览器中逐篇点击保存，难以顺畅衔接批量研究流。 **Agentero 并非旨在替代 Zotero，而是探索一种人与 Agent 协同处理科研上下文的新方式**： * **人类负责**：提出研究问题、进行学术价值判断、深度研读与核心结论推导； * **Agent 负责**：批量检索筛选、元数据抓取、图表与公式提取、引用关系梳理及基础总结。 --- ## 核心功能 ### 1. 结构化阅读与笔记系统 * **PDF 阅读与批注**：提供大纲导航、整页与宽度自适应、平滑划词、高亮批注与全文检索。 * **图表与公式提取**：自动解析论文中的数学公式、算法伪代码及表格，生成结构化 Markdown 与 LaTeX 内容，确保 Agent 调用时上下文准确无误。 * **双向链接笔记**：内置所见即所得 Markdown 编辑器，支持 `[[双链]]` 引用语法、`/` 快捷指令与 LaTeX 实时渲染，笔记与文献建立原生关联。 * **多模式翻译服务**：支持划词翻译、按页对照翻译与全文翻译，内置可用翻译通道，并支持配置自定义 API Key（BYOK）。


分屏阅读与分析：左侧高亮批注，右侧本地 Agent 基于准确的结构化上下文进行答疑与推导

Paxeer X Network is one network with two execution domains: the Paxeer X chain (`paxd`, Go, EVM chain ID 125) and the LayerX kernel (`layerxd`, C17), the deterministic execution and accounting domain for autonomous agents. This repository is its monorepo: the chain node, the LayerX kernel, the on-chain contracts, the off-chain services, the client SDKs and the user-facing applications. Official site: [paxeer.network](https://paxeer.network/). Documentation: [docs.paxeer.app](https://docs.paxeer.app/). It runs on Ruby's standard library by default, it supports concurrent and parallel tool execution and has a single coherent API that spans 15+ providers. The README covers a lot of ground and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) tracks what has changed between releases. ## Install ##### v17 The v17 series requires Ruby 3.4 or later.
```bash gem install llm.rb ``` ##### v18 The v18 series is available as a prerelease.
It requires Ruby 4.0.0 or later. Ruby 4.1.0+ is recommended. ```bash gem install llm.rb --pre ``` ## Quick start ### Agents The [`LLM::Agent`](https://r.uby.dev/api-docs/llm.rb/LLM/Agent.html) class is the default high-level interface, and it is recommended for most use-cases. It manages the tool loop and provides configurable features on top of it. For example you can manage the tool loop with a retry budget and a tool call budget - alongside other features. The runtime is designed to keep the tool loop alive and it will rescue exceptions. When an exception is encountered in a tool it is reported back to the model as an in-band error that allows the model to change course or retry with different parameters. # Overflow ## Who this is for You spent Tuesday evening fixing someone else's flaky test. The bug in your own tracker just turned eleven months old. You had time to help then. You need help now. What if that Tuesday could pay for it? **Let your spare weeks pay for the dry ones.** Overflow is a shared ledger for open-source work, for people and small teams whose capacity comes and goes. When you have leftover LLM subscription usage that you won't burn on your own projects, work on others' issues and earn credit. Spend it on your own backlog when you're depleted. No money changes hands. There is no token. ## Where to register Go to <https://overflow.nitjsefni.eu> and sign in with GitHub. Register a repository you administer on one form: the repository and its two label catalogs. The catalog labels must already exist. Overflow installs the webhook for you. GitHub repositories register in one of two ways. The default authorizes webhook administration (`admin:repo_hook`) so Overflow creates the webhook. Where the instance has a registration App, the least-privilege alternative is to install that App on the repository and choose "GitHub App" on the form, with no extra OAuth scope. See [API.md](API.md#programmatic-repository-registration) for the API form. **You don't need a repository to start earning.** Take an issue in one that's already registered. This repository is on that ledger too. You can watch the exchange happen in its own tracker. ## How it works 1. A repository sponsor puts a price on an issue with an opening label. 2. An outside contributor does the work and opens a pull request that closes the issue. 3. Between the closing PR's final commit and merge, the sponsor confirms the price with an actual-catalog label and a comment naming it. 4. The PR merges. github.text_excerpt: # Hive [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14261/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14261) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) Hive is a co-maintainer for your GitHub project that never sleeps. Point it at a repo, set the limits, and let short-lived AI agents handle the maintenance chores while humans keep the decisions that matter. ## What Hive is Hive watches the work that piles up in a repository — issues, pull requests, failing CI, CVEs, and dependabot alerts — and sends AI coding agents (Claude, Copilot, Codex, Antigravity, Goose…) to deal with it: triage, fixes, reviews, releases. You decide how much it is allowed to do. Humans keep every decision that matters; agents do the chores. ## "I already use an agent. How is this different?" A terminal agent is a power tool: you hold it, aim it, and it stops when you stop. Hive is the workshop that runs the power tools for you — on three rules the industry is only now discovering: 1. **Short-lived agents.** Every task starts a fresh agent with a clean context and ends it. No "long-running" agent drifting for hours. 2. **External context.** What the agent needs to know lives outside the model — in your repo, your knowledge base, your audit trail — and is re-injected each time, so nothing is forgotten and nothing is hallucinated from stale memory. 3. **Prompts driven by deterministic facts.** The instructions an agent gets are templates filled from real data (the issue, the CI log, the diff, the trust level), not hand-tuned prose. Around that, Hive picks work from your real queue, sets limits in code with six trust levels from the **AI Codebase Maturity Model (ACMM)** — a framework for how much autonomy a codebase is ready to give agents ([levels](#acmm-levels) · [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09388)), checks before and after with deterministic filters and gates, writes every action to an audit log owned by a named human, and runs around the clock. Same agents you use today — governed, scheduled, scoped, and accountable. ## Hub and spoke - **Spoke** — one running Hive, serving your repo(s). It is where agents actually work. aihot.text_excerpt:
感谢IT之家网友 Stephen_233 、 乌蝇哥的左手 、 补药吖 的线索投递！ IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，OpenAI 宣布，其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项重大突破，展现出 AI 独立发现并证明复杂科学理论的能力，而不只是回答问题或辅助研究。 在数学领域，AI 证明了适用于所有维度的局部光滑猜想，并由此解决 局部光滑猜想与挂谷猜想 。 在计算机科学领域，AI 推翻了 长期被广泛接受的指数时间假设 ，意味着未来可能找到速度更快的算法。 在物理学领域，AI 提出 量子色动力学及杨–米尔斯理论的严格数学存在性证明 ，涉及世界七大千禧年数学难题之一。 OpenAI 表示，数学和计算机科学成果已通过 Lean 数学验证工具进行形式化验证，并公开证明材料；物理学成果正由诺贝尔物理学奖得主等专家参与审查。相关成果仍需学术界进一步独立确认。 IT之家附上 OpenAI On September 9, 2026, Cloudflare notified us of cross-request KV cache exposure in its GLM-5.3 deployment on Workers AI. We worked with Cloudflare to address the request-rejection path involved and strengthen related cache-lifetime handling in disaggregated serving. We are publishing this disclosure in coordination with Cloudflare and the researcher who reported the issue through Cloudflare’s HackerOne program. Cloudflare’s report covers its production incident and customer impact, and the researcher’s report (available soon) will describe the discovery and external validation. This post focuses on the underlying mechanisms, the changes we made, and guidance for SGLang operators. Read Cloudflare’s report here. Impact and affected deployments Cloudflare reports that the incident affected @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3 on Workers AI between August 27 and September 9, 2026. Its investigation found no other Workers AI model affected. Cloudflare’s investigation found that requests exceeding the prefill KV cache capacity could return content from another user’s session. For details on the incident’s scope and customer impact, see Cloudflare’s incident report. The issue occurred in disaggregated prefill/decode serving, where separate workers process the prompt and generate the response. The single-node rejection path returned an error instead. What happened Cloudflare’s deployment had a configured context length of 1,048,576 tokens, but its prefill KV cache pool could hold 681,280 tokens.
